title: How the king moves
outcomes: Taps the squares a king can step to, never onto an attacked square or next to the enemy king
Decides whether the king can take a neighbouring piece by checking whether it is guarded
Ignores a distant enemy piece that attacks none of the squares around the king

steps.text: The **king** moves one square in any direction. He is the piece you must never lose, so there is one extra rule: **a king may never move onto a square the enemy attacks** (a square where an enemy piece could capture).

steps.caption: The black rook attacks the whole fifth rank. The king cannot step onto it.

steps.text: Two kings can never stand on neighbouring squares either: each would attack the other's square. So the squares around the enemy king are off limits, even if no other piece attacks them.

The king can capture too, but only if the piece is not guarded. A piece is **guarded** (or defended) when a friendly piece could recapture on its square. **When it holds:** step to free or safely capturable squares. **When it fails:** an attacked square, a square next to the enemy king, or a guarded piece. Ask before you capture: which enemy pieces attack the square I am about to land on?
